newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan grain buyers see no impact from US sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Japan grain buyers see no impact from US sanctions.

text.p: Japan's trade houses and shipping firms said on Thursday they do not expect any immediate impact on grain imports from a U.S. decision to impose retaliatory surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports.
"Their targets are container vessels, not bulk carriers which are used for imports of grain such as corn and soybean. We see no immediate impact at this stage," an official of a shipping firm said.

The U.S. Federal Maritime Commission said on Wednesday it would impose $100,000 surcharges on vessels from April 14, in response to what it termed "unfavourable restrictive practices" at Japanese ports.

The commission said the surcharge would be imposed each time a vessel owned or operated by Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd or Nippon Yusen KK enters a U.S. port from abroad, but not from another U.S. port.
Some trade houses expressed concern about the impact of sanctions on the rice trade, since Japan currently imports rice via container ship.
Japan is the largest buyer of U.S. grains, including corn, soybean and wheat.
